To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) the NDLTD catalog is of high quality and (2) a simple keyword-based filtering method is sufficient to filter out most non-computing related entries

(1) the quality of metadata in the NDLTD Union Catalog is high and can be used to build a sub-collection of ETDs that are of interest to computing scholars, and (2) the quality of this sub-collection can be improved further using a combination of different sources of evidence.

the NDLTD Union Catalog is an important source of computing-related theses and disserta-tions, that the metadata quality of this OAI Union Catalog is not as high as we would have liked, and that the combination of multiple evidence sources is a good strategy to improve the accuracy of filtering out non-computing-related entries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how to use OAI metadata to build a filtering service for the CITIDEL collection of computing related resources.
how to improve the quality of metadata and the accuracy of the filtering process, and how to improve the user experience of the CITIDEL service.

two main questions: (1) how can the NDLTD be used to improve the coverage of the CITIDEL collection?; and (2) how can a filtering service be designed to improve the quality of the NLDLTD collection for the CITIDEL?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a filtering service for CITIDEL based on NDLTD is feasible.
the OAI-based filtering service is a useful tool that can help to increase the size of CITIDEL.
the NDLTD metadata is of good quality and that the filtering experiments have produced a sub-collection of ETDs of good quality that can be added to the CITIDEL collection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the filtering process was successful in identifying the majority of computing related ETDs in the NDLTD catalog and that the accuracy of the filtering process was improved when using multiple sources of evidence.
, while there are some issues in the metadata quality, the filtering service is able to identify with reasonable accuracy computing related ETDs from NDLTD OAC.
the filtering process is not a simple one.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the metadata quality of NDLTD OAi records is not sufficient for automatic classification.
a combination of metadata analysis, citation analysis, and manual review is necessary to achieve a high level of accuracy for filtering computing related ETDs from NDLTD.
a combination of metadata quality analysis, manual inspection and automatic filtering is a good approach to extract a sub-collection of ETDs for a particular domain.
